note: Textbook construction classes keyed by (dataset_id, h11, h21). These are class-level examples — many distinct geometries can share the same Hodge numbers.

constructions.name: Quintic threefold in ℂP⁴
constructions.note: Textbook example. Many distinct quintics share (h¹¹,h²¹)=(1,101).

constructions.name: Mirror quintic
constructions.ambient: Toric mirror of P^4[5] (Greene–Plesser orbifold / KS dual)
constructions.hypersurface_equation: Mirror family of the quintic (orbifold + resolution)
constructions.note: Hodge mirror of the quintic: (h¹¹,h²¹)=(101,1), χ=+200.

constructions.name: Bicubic in P²×P²
constructions.note: Pedagogical example with h¹¹=2, h²¹=83, χ=−162.

constructions.name: CICY P⁵[2,4]
constructions.hypersurface_equation: Complete intersection of a quadric and a quartic in P^5

constructions.name: CICY P⁵[3,3]
constructions.hypersurface_equation: Complete intersection of two cubics in P^5

constructions.name: Hypersurface in P³×P¹
constructions.note: Class-level ambient sketch; confirm weights before phenomenological use.

constructions.name: Weighted octic WP⁴[1,1,1,1,4]
constructions.hypersurface_equation: Degree-8 hypersurface in weighted projective space
constructions.note: Famous weighted projective example near the quintic locus in Hodge space.

constructions.name: Tetraquadric in (P¹)⁴
constructions.note: Often used in mirror-symmetry and Picard–Fuchs pedagogy.

constructions.name: Elliptic fibration over P² (large CS)

constructions.name: Self-mirror Hodge locus (χ=0)
constructions.note: h¹¹=h²¹ ⇒ χ=0. Many distinct geometries; listed as a Hodge-class landmark only.
